title: Multi-Tenant Application Security with Tenant Isolation
question: Design a security system for a multi-tenant SaaS application where each tenant's data must be completely isolated. Requirements: 1) Implement authentication where users belong to specific tenants and can only access their tenant's data, 2) Support tenant-specific roles (tenant_admin, tenant_user) plus super_admin who can access all tenants, 3) Automatically filter all database queries by tenant_id based on authenticated user's tenant, 4) Prevent privilege escalation where users try to access other tenants' data by manipulating request parameters, 5) Support tenant-specific JWT tokens containing tenant context, 6) Handle tenant onboarding with initial admin user creation. Discuss: storing tenant_id in SecurityContext and making it available throughout request lifecycle, implementing custom UserDetails with tenant information, using @PreAuthorize with SpEL to check tenant access (e.g., @PreAuthorize("@tenantSecurity.checkAccess(#tenantId)")), implementing JPA @Filter or @Where to automatically add tenant_id to all queries, using ThreadLocal for tenant context, protecting against tenant_id manipulation in requests, handling super_admin with special tenant=* logic, JWT claims for tenant_id, and database-level row-level security as additional defense layer.

title: Microservices Security with Service-to-Service Authentication
question: Design security architecture for a microservices ecosystem with 20+ services. Requirements: 1) Users authenticate once at API Gateway and subsequent service-to-service calls are authenticated, 2) Implement different security models: JWT for user-facing APIs, OAuth2 client credentials for service-to-service communication, 3) Services must validate tokens and enforce their own authorization rules based on scopes/roles, 4) Handle token propagation through service call chains while preventing token theft, 5) Support both synchronous (REST) and asynchronous (Kafka) communication patterns with security, 6) Implement rate limiting and threat detection at gateway level. Discuss: using API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway) for centralized authentication and token issuance, propagating JWT through service chain via RequestInterceptor/WebClient filters, implementing OAuth2 Resource Server in each microservice for token validation, using service mesh (Istio) for mTLS between services, storing shared JWT signing keys in distributed config (Spring Cloud Config), implementing token relay pattern vs new token generation at each hop, handling token expiration in long-running async operations, using OAuth2 scopes for fine-grained service permissions, circuit breaker impact on security (should fail closed), and centralized audit logging with correlation IDs.

title: Social Login Integration with Multiple OAuth2 Providers
question: Implement social login allowing users to sign in with Google, Facebook, GitHub, and traditional email/password. Requirements: 1) Users can link multiple social accounts to single application account, 2) First social login creates user account; subsequent logins from same email link accounts, 3) Support account merging when user logs in with different providers using same email, 4) Handle cases where OAuth2 provider doesn't return email (Twitter), 5) Store OAuth2 tokens for making API calls to provider on behalf of user, 6) Implement account unlinking and security considerations, 7) Support both web (Authorization Code flow) and mobile (PKCE) clients. Discuss: using Spring Security OAuth2 Client with multiple ClientRegistration configurations, implementing custom OAuth2UserService to handle user creation/lookup/linking, storing provider-specific user IDs in user_oauth_connections table, handling email conflicts with manual verification step, refreshing stored OAuth2 tokens, implementing OAuth2AuthorizedClientService for token storage (database vs in-memory), security of token storage (encryption), handling provider changes (scope changes, token revocation), allowing users to unlink with validation (must keep at least one auth method), using custom OAuth2AuthenticationSuccessHandler for post-login logic, and CSRF protection with OAuth2 state parameter.

title: Dynamic Role-Based Access Control with Permissions
question: Design a flexible RBAC system where roles and permissions can be created/modified at runtime without code changes. Requirements: 1) Support hierarchical roles (Manager inherits Employee permissions), 2) Fine-grained permissions (user.create, user.read, user.update, user.delete), 3) Resource-level permissions (user can edit only their own posts vs admin can edit all), 4) Permission checking in controllers, services, and UI (show/hide buttons), 5) Performance: avoid N+1 queries when loading user permissions, 6) Admin UI for managing roles and permissions. Discuss: database schema with user, role, permission, user_roles, role_permissions tables, implementing custom PermissionEvaluator for @PreAuthorize("hasPermission('POST', 'DELETE')"), loading all user permissions at login and storing in SecurityContext to avoid repeated DB queries, using @PostFilter to filter collections based on ownership, implementing custom GrantedAuthority that includes permissions, caching role-permission mappings with eviction on admin changes, handling permission hierarchy with recursive CTE or role_hierarchy table, method security expressions with custom beans (e.g., @PreAuthorize("@postSecurity.canEdit(#postId)")), performance optimization with Redis caching of user permissions, and UI integration with sec:authorize in Thymeleaf or custom security service in Angular/React.

title: Secure File Upload with Virus Scanning and Access Control
question: Implement secure file upload system with comprehensive security controls. Requirements: 1) Validate file types, sizes, and content (not just extension), 2) Scan uploaded files for viruses/malware before storing, 3) Store files outside web root with access control (users can only access their own files), 4) Generate signed URLs with expiration for file downloads, 5) Support large file uploads (multi-part, resumable), 6) Prevent directory traversal and other injection attacks, 7) Audit log of all file operations (upload, download, delete). Discuss: validating file content with Apache Tika (MIME type detection based on content, not extension), using ClamAV or VirusTotal API for virus scanning, quarantining uploaded files during scan, storing files in S3/MinIO with UUID filenames to prevent enumeration, implementing custom file download controller with @PreAuthorize checking ownership, generating pre-signed URLs with expiration using JWT or HMAC signatures, handling file uploads with multipart size limits, implementing resumable uploads with chunking, preventing path traversal with input validation and canonicalization, CSP headers to prevent uploaded HTML/SVG from executing scripts, storing file metadata (original name, MIME type, owner) in database separately, using @Async for virus scanning to not block upload response, and comprehensive audit trail with user, file, operation, timestamp in audit log.

title: API Rate Limiting and Throttling with Spring Security
question: Implement API rate limiting to prevent abuse and ensure fair usage. Requirements: 1) Different rate limits per user tier (free: 100 req/hour, premium: 1000 req/hour, enterprise: unlimited), 2) Track both per-user and per-IP rate limits, 3) Support burst allowance (allow short bursts above limit), 4) Return clear error responses with retry-after header when limit exceeded, 5) Implement rate limiting for both authenticated and anonymous users, 6) Admin endpoints to view and reset rate limits, 7) Distributed rate limiting across multiple server instances. Discuss: implementing custom RateLimitingFilter before authentication filter, using Redis with sliding window algorithm (ZSET with timestamp scores), per-user limits stored as user attribute and checked with @PreAuthorize, token bucket algorithm for burst handling, returning 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header, using IP-based rate limiting for anonymous users with X-Forwarded-For handling, implementing RateLimiter service with annotations like @RateLimited(limit=100, window=3600), distributed rate limiting with Redis INCR and EXPIRE, handling Redis failures (fail-open vs fail-closed), performance impact of rate limit checks, using Spring AOP for declarative rate limiting, rate limit by API endpoint groups (writes vs reads), and monitoring/alerting on users hitting limits frequently.

title: Strong Password Policy with History and Complexity
question: Implement comprehensive password security policies. Requirements: 1) Enforce password complexity (min length 12, uppercase, lowercase, number, special char), 2) Prevent password reuse (check against last 10 passwords), 3) Implement password expiration (90 days) with grace period, 4) Account lockout after 5 failed attempts with exponential backoff, 5) Support password reset with secure token (one-time, expiring), 6) Implement multi-factor authentication (TOTP), 7) Detect and prevent common/breached passwords (HaveIBeenPwned API). Discuss: implementing custom PasswordValidator with complexity rules, storing password hashes with BCrypt (never plaintext), storing password history in separate table with user_id and password_hash, comparing new password against history before allowing change, implementing password_expires_at column with periodic check, building custom AuthenticationFailureHandler to track failed attempts, storing failed_login_attempts and locked_until in user table, implementing exponential backoff (5 min, 15 min, 1 hour), password reset with crypto-secure random token stored in password_reset_tokens table with expiration, implementing TOTP with Google Authenticator using libraries like jbcrypt, storing TOTP secrets encrypted in database, checking passwords against HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity API, forcing password change on first login or after expiration, and sending security notifications on password changes.

title: Comprehensive Security Audit Logging and Compliance
question: Implement security audit logging for compliance requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, GDPR). Requirements: 1) Log all authentication events (login, logout, failed attempts), 2) Log all authorization failures (403 errors with user, resource, action), 3) Log sensitive data access (viewing user profiles, downloading reports), 4) Ensure audit logs are tamper-proof and cannot be modified, 5) Support querying audit logs by user, action, resource, date range, 6) Retain audit logs for 7 years with efficient storage, 7) Alert on suspicious patterns (multiple failed logins, privilege escalation attempts). Discuss: implementing custom AuthenticationSuccessHandler and AuthenticationFailureHandler for login auditing, using Spring AOP with @Around advice to automatically audit @PreAuthorize failures, creating AuditLog entity with user_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, ip_address, timestamp, success status, using @Async to write audit logs without impacting request performance, storing audit logs in append-only table with database-level permissions preventing updates/deletes, partitioning audit_log table by month for performance, implementing @Audited annotation for sensitive operations with custom AuditAspect, using separate database or log aggregation system (ELK stack) for audit logs to prevent deletion, encrypting sensitive data in audit logs, implementing audit log search API with pagination and filtering, analyzing patterns with scheduled jobs to detect anomalies (10 failed logins in 5 minutes triggers alert), GDPR considerations (logging IP addresses, right to erasure), and immutable audit trail with digital signatures or blockchain for high-security environments.

title: API Key Management for External Integrations
question: Implement API key based authentication for external partner integrations. Requirements: 1) Generate cryptographically secure API keys for partners, 2) Support API key rotation without service interruption, 3) Different permission scopes per API key (read-only, read-write, admin), 4) Track API usage per key for billing and analytics, 5) Implement API key revocation and expiration, 6) Support both header-based (X-API-Key) and query parameter authentication, 7) Secure storage and transmission of API keys. Discuss: generating API keys with SecureRandom and encoding as base64/hex (min 32 bytes entropy), storing hashed API keys in database (never plaintext) using BCrypt, implementing custom ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter that extracts key from header, validating hashed key against database, implementing ApiKey entity with partner_id, key_hash, scopes, created_at, expires_at, last_used_at, supporting key rotation by allowing multiple active keys per partner with automatic cleanup of old keys after grace period, using @PreAuthorize to check API key scopes (e.g., @PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('SCOPE_write')")), tracking API usage in api_usage_log table with key_id, endpoint, timestamp for billing calculations, implementing rate limiting per API key, supporting key revocation with is_revoked flag and immediate effect, warning partners before key expiration, HTTPS-only enforcement for API key transmission, preventing key exposure in URLs (prefer headers), allowing partners to regenerate keys through self-service portal, and monitoring for suspicious API key usage patterns (key used from multiple IPs, unusual traffic patterns).

title: Zero Trust Security Model Implementation
question: Implement zero trust security principles in a Spring application. Requirements: 1) Every request is authenticated and authorized (no implicit trust), 2) Verify user, device, and location for each request, 3) Implement step-up authentication for sensitive operations (require MFA even if already logged in), 4) Continuous authentication with session risk scoring, 5) Network segmentation with service-to-service authentication, 6) Implement least privilege access with just-in-time permissions, 7) Comprehensive logging and monitoring of all access. Discuss: disabling session-based authentication in favor of JWT on every request, implementing device fingerprinting with DeviceDetector library, storing device_id and requiring device verification for new devices, checking IP geolocation and flagging suspicious locations, implementing risk scoring based on user behavior (new device +50 points, unusual location +30 points, after-hours access +20 points), requiring step-up MFA when risk score exceeds threshold or for sensitive operations (PasswordEncoder.matches() + TOTP check), using short-lived JWT tokens (5-15 minutes) with refresh tokens, implementing continuous authentication by re-validating critical claims on each request, service-to-service mTLS with certificate verification, implementing just-in-time access where users request temporary elevated permissions with time-bound grants, using @PreAuthorize with time checks (e.g., @PreAuthorize("@accessGrantService.hasActiveGrant(authentication, 'ADMIN')")), comprehensive audit logging of all access with risk scores, monitoring with SIEM integration, and implementing adaptive authentication that adjusts security requirements based on risk.
